bull_bear.body:
- Consultative, advisory-led approach backed by deep industry expertise and strong insurer relationships
- Long-standing relationships with over 2,000 corporate clients across diverse industries, supporting strong client retention
- Workplace distribution model reaching nearly 10 lakh employees for personalised retail insurance advisory and digital engagement
- More than two decades of trusted relationships across insurers and reinsurers globally in the Reinsurance business, with specialised technical expertise, high barriers to entry and a lean operating model
- Regional platform spanning India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Kenya and Singapore supporting cross-border risk placements and regional expansion
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Pricing pressure, claims inflation and fraud risk in Indian motor insurance — Motor insurance remains a large, stable segment for the Group but pricing pressure, claims inflation, fraud risk and cost-efficiency challenges continue to affect profitability, requiring the mix to shift toward health, MSME, liability, cyber and specialty lines for future profitable growth.
- Softening global commercial insurance pricing — Marsh's Global Insurance Market Index reported a 4% decline in global commercial insurance rates in Q2 2025, the fourth consecutive quarterly decline, with property, cyber and financial/professional lines seeing softer pricing across regions — a cyclical pressure on broker and insurer economics.
- Rising natural catastrophe and climate-related losses — Munich Re reported global natural catastrophe losses of approximately USD 320 billion in 2024 (USD 140 billion insured), underscoring a widening protection gap and increasing relevance of climate risk, storms, floods and hurricanes for underwriting discipline and reinsurance capacity that the Group's brokerage and reinsurance businesses depend on.
- Geopolitical and trade-policy uncertainty — Geopolitical tensions (particularly in the Middle East), continuing US-China trade uncertainty, tariff-related measures and export controls could disrupt energy infrastructure, shipping routes and global supply chains, affecting commodity prices, freight costs, business confidence and cross-border trade relevant to the Group's international operations.
- Multi-country emerging-market currency and macro exposure — The Group operates across India, Sri Lanka, Maldives and Kenya; emerging and developing economies are projected to grow only 3.9%-4.2% and remain exposed to external financing conditions, currency volatility and commodity price movements, creating cross-border earnings and translation risk.
- Kenya market-specific claims and affordability pressures — The Kenyan insurance market faces motor claims leakage, medical inflation and affordability constraints, requiring strong analytics, disciplined underwriting, claims oversight and embedded-insurance partnerships to sustain growth.
- Moderating global insurance premium growth — Global insurance premium growth is expected to moderate to approximately 2.0% in 2025 and 2.3% in 2026 (Swiss Re Institute) after a strong 2024 rebound, reflecting slower global economic growth, policy uncertainty and affordability pressures in inflation-sensitive segments such as motor, construction and property.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: IIRM Holdings India Limited is an insurance and reinsurance broking and risk-management group operating through Corporate Insurance, Retail Insurance and Reinsurance businesses. It serves over 2,000 corporate clients across diverse industries and reaches nearly 10 lakh employees through a workplace distribution model for retail insurance, while its Reinsurance division facilitates complex cross-border risk placements with insurers and reinsurers globally.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Corporate Insurance:** Employee Benefits, Property, Marine, Liability, Engineering, Project Insurance, Cyber Insurance, M&A Insurance
- **Retail Insurance:** Motor insurance, Health insurance, Life insurance, Protection products
- **Reinsurance:** Cross-border reinsurance placement / broking
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- India Insure Risk Management & Insurance Broking Services Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) Indian subsidiary, insurance broking services; acquired January 18, 2024
- IIRM Global Shared Services Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) Indian subsidiary providing shared services; formerly I Share Business Services India Private Limited; acquired January 18, 2024
- IIRM Wellness Services Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) Indian subsidiary; formerly Evexia Solutions Private Limited; acquired January 18, 2024
- IIRM Holdings Pte Ltd, Singapore — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) overseas holding subsidiary; acts as holding entity for the Group's Sri Lanka and Maldives step-down subsidiaries and Kenya associate; acquired January 18, 2024
- IIRM Lanka Insurance Brokers Private Limited, Sri Lanka — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary held 83.19% by IIRM Holdings Pte Ltd, Singapore; insurance broking
- IIRM Maldives Insurance Brokers Private Limited, Maldives — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary held 75% by IIRM Holdings Pte Ltd, Singapore; insurance broking
- IIRM Kenya Insurance Brokers Limited, Kenya — associate: Associate company held 40% by IIRM Holdings Pte Ltd, Singapore, via equity holding; not consolidated as holding is only 40%; insurance broking
- Sampada Business Solutions Limited — related party: Former wholly owned subsidiary, amalgamated (as Transferor Company) into IIRM Holdings India Limited pursuant to Scheme of Amalgamation approved by the Regional Director, South East Region, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Hyderabad, order dated July 22, 2025; no longer a separate entity

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Deepen advisory capabilities across Corporate, MSME, Retail and Specialty segments
- Expand health and employee benefits solutions across geographies
- Strengthen MSME, specialty, liability and cyber insurance lines
- Enhance analytics and claims management capabilities
- Leverage digital platforms and technology-driven innovation to improve customer experience and operational efficiency
- Improve cost efficiency and support product innovation
- Build robust insurer, reinsurer and risk-management partnerships across geographies
- Shift Retail Insurance from a volume-driven, motor-led mix toward higher-margin health, life and protection products
- Pursue disciplined inorganic growth (M&A) alongside organic growth to enter new markets, strengthen specialised capabilities and enhance scale
- Expand presence across India and international markets (Sri Lanka, Maldives, Kenya, Singapore) to support regional expansion
- After considering the Company's working capital requirements and capital expenditure plans, the Board did not recommend any dividend for FY26, and no amount was transferred to the General Reserve during the year, indicating a policy of retaining earnings to fund working capital and growth investment over near-term shareholder payout.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: IIRM Holdings' expansion is capability- and geography-led rather than plant-based, consistent with an asset-light insurance broking model. During FY26 the Group invested in technology platforms, digital capabilities and CRM transformation to improve customer experience, operational efficiency and scalable digital infrastructure, and continued building its Retail Insurance workplace distribution model (reaching nearly 10 lakh employees). The corporate structure was also reorganised via the amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary Sampada Business Solutions Limited into IIRM Holdings India Limited (approved by the Regional Director, South East Region, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Hyderabad, order dated 22 July 2025), which also increased the Company's authorised share capital. Going forward, management has flagged inorganic growth (acquisitions) as a key pillar to enter new markets and add specialised capabilities, alongside continued organic expansion across its existing India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Kenya and Singapore footprint.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- General insurance industry across the Group's operating geographies offers a favourable long-term growth outlook, supported by low insurance penetration, sustained economic growth, infrastructure investment and rising protection awareness
- Regulatory reforms and digital penetration are expanding insurance access and encouraging structured risk management across individuals, MSMEs and corporates
- Platform-led distribution, data analytics, automation and enhanced claims servicing are reshaping the insurance value chain, favouring brokers with technology-enabled service models
- In India, health insurance is gaining prominence on medical inflation, group insurance demand, employer-sponsored benefits and retail protection needs; future profitable growth is expected to be driven by health, MSME, liability, cyber and specialty lines rather than motor, which faces pricing pressure, claims inflation and fraud risk
- Sri Lanka's insurance market is recovering with broker-channel opportunities emerging in corporate insurance, project-linked covers, health benefits and risk advisory as the market normalises
- Maldives presents niche, high-growth opportunities linked to tourism, hospitality, marine activity and climate-related exposures, with disciplined reinsurance support central to market stability
- Kenya offers growth through digital adoption, mobile money ecosystems, medical insurance demand, agriculture-linked protection and microinsurance, alongside challenges from motor claims leakage and medical inflation
- Global insurance premium growth is moderating and commercial insurance pricing has softened, but clients increasingly seek expert broker guidance on coverage complexity, claims inflation and emerging risks (cyber, climate), which is expected to keep broker demand resilient
- Reinsurance business saw temporary moderation during the year due to regulatory changes but management remains optimistic on its long-term potential given specialised expertise, high barriers to entry and stable contractual revenue streams
- Continued investment in digital platforms and CRM transformation is expected to enhance productivity, client engagement and analytics capability, supporting margin performance over the medium to long term
